Abstract
10
Regulatory assignments depend on association inputs and signal models. We screened 5,460 of
11
6,923 primary biliary cholangitis locus-gene-cell comparisons and evaluated a protocol-frozen 642-
12
comparison subset. Matching variant support and disease statistics changed 15 and 19 classifications,
13
respectively. Eight shared-signal (H4) calls became distinct-signal (H3), and ten changed conversely.
14
Shared and distinct pairs coexisted in 32 of 92 H4-supported comparisons, while a FCRL3 T-cell
15
assignment reversed between covariate models. Across 486,000 simulations, multi-signal inference
16
reduced false sharing from 12.41% to 8.56% and shared-signal recovery from 32.99% to 26.66%;
17
only 33.08% were pair-evaluable. IL12RB2 sharing in natural killer cells received external disease-
18
study and chromatin support, whereas liver data showed detectability without corrected disease
19
enrichment. These results support signal-specific, model-qualified regulatory attribution without
20
establishing mediation or universal methodological superiority.
21
Keywords: primary biliary cholangitis; colocalization; single-cell eQTL; fine-mapping; linkage
22
disequilibrium; signal pair; regulatory genomics; statistical genetics
23
Introduction
24
Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is an autoimmune cholestatic liver disease characterized by
25
progressive injury to small intrahepatic bile ducts [1]. Genome-wide association studies have
26
identified a substantial inherited component and many non-HLA susceptibility loci, creating a
27
strong foundation for mechanistic prioritization [2]. The central interpretive problem is no longer
28
whether associated regions exist. It is whether a regional disease association and a molecular
29
quantitative-trait locus (QTL) implicate the same local signal, in which gene and cellular context,
30
and with what degree of uncertainty. Functional follow-up depends on resolving that uncertainty: a
31
strongly associated gene in the wrong cell context can direct experiments toward a regulatory
32
assignment that the genetic data do not support.
33
Single-cell QTL resources make this problem biologically more specific. OneK1K mapped cell-
34
type-specific genetic effects on gene expression in peripheral blood immune populations [3], and
35
TenK10K extends immune-cell molecular-QTL mapping to a larger donor cohort and a broader
36
cellular taxonomy [4]. These resources allow the same disease locus to be compared across genes
37
and cell contexts. That resolution also increases statistical dependence: a locus can contain several
38

2
disease and expression signals, the same gene can appear in related immune populations, and a
39
comparison-level label can conceal different signal pairs.
40
Approximate Bayes factor (ABF) colocalization provides an efficient first-pass test of whether two
41
association patterns are more compatible with one shared causal variant (H4) or with two distinct
42
causal variants (H3) [5]. Its standard formulation assumes at most one causal variant per trait in the
43
tested region. That assumption can be restrictive in autoimmune loci with allelic heterogeneity.
44
Multi-signal fine-mapping and signal-pair colocalization can instead represent several local
45
components [6,7], but a direct comparison is difficult when the procedures use different variant sets,
46
disease summaries or linkage disequilibrium (LD) inputs. An apparent H4-to-H3 or H3-to-H4
47
change can then reflect input mismatch as well as inferential structure.
48
This distinction matters for biological attribution. A stable shared signal pair supports a locus-gene-
49
cell regulatory association, but it does not prove expression mediation or a molecular mechanism. A
50
stable distinct pair does not imply that the entire locus contains no shared signal. Indeed, shared and
51
distinct signal pairs can coexist within one locus-gene-cell comparison. Model sensitivity can also
52
be informative: it identifies assignments that depend on the covariate adjustment used to construct
53
QTL summaries and model-matched LD, rather than providing a reason to select the configuration
54
that yields the most favorable posterior.
55
We used PBC to test the reliability of immune-cell regulatory attribution through a linked sequence
56
of questions. A PBC-wide screen defined a bounded high-information subset. Matched-input single-
57
causal arms then distinguished changes caused by variant support and disease-statistic definitions
58
from differences remaining between complete inferential procedures. Signal-pair identity and
59
covariate sensitivity established what a comparison-level label could mean. Truth-known
60
simulations tested the trade-off between false sharing, recovery and credible-set discovery. Finally,
61
representative FCRL3 B-cell and IL12RB2-NK assignments were examined across molecular-QTL
62
resources, a different disease study system, linked chromatin and donor-level liver expression. This
63
design asked which assignments persisted, why others changed, and where statistical support
64
stopped short of mechanism.
65
Results
66
PBC-wide screening defined a bounded high-information multi-signal analysis
67
The frozen registry contained 6,923 locus-gene-cell comparisons. Of these, 5,460 met the overlap
68
threshold for ABF screening and 1,463 were coverage-insufficient (Figure 1a). The latter were not
69
interpreted as negative colocalization results. The multi-signal workload contained 642 comparisons:
70
184 primary trigger-verification comparisons, 455 H3 rescue/falsification comparisons and three
71
borderline calibration cases (Figure 1d). It covered 47 PBC regions, 200 genes, 14 cell types and
72
286 cell-locus blocks. Complete records are provided in Source Data 1, S2/. The four-arm input
73
contract is shown in Figure 1b; the complete adjacent transition matrices are provided in
74
Supplementary Figure S1.
75
The final PF10 multi-signal classification contained 92 H4-supported comparisons, 428 H3-
76
supported comparisons, 59 model-sensitive comparisons and 63 uninformative comparisons (Figure
77
1c). These are comparison counts, not independent genes or loci. The 92 H4-supported comparisons
78

3

79
cell-context resolution but did not create additional independent disease associations. The H4-
80
supported fraction describes this selected workload and is not an estimated prevalence across all
81
PBC regulatory comparisons.

Input matching explained part of the bidirectional reclassification
95
The actual multi-signal support S_M was smaller than the historical ABF support S_A in all 642
96
comparisons, with 19-114 variants removed per comparison (median 65; median 7.67%; Figure 2a).
97
A0 replay reproduced the historical ABF posteriors to within 3.55x10^-13, establishing numerical
98
identity before attribution.
99
Restricting the ABF calculation from S_A to S_M changed 15 categorical states (A0-to-A1) while
100
retaining all 112 historical H4 states. Replacing the harmonized GCST disease definition with the
101
matched GJOKA z-statistic definition changed 19 states (A1-to-A2; Figure 2b). Fixed-versus-native
102
sdY and matched-z-versus-rounded GJOKA sensitivity definitions produced no categorical changes
103
within the frozen 642. The two change counts can involve the same comparisons and are not
104
additive.
105
After exact support and disease-statistic matching, comparison with the frozen multi-signal result
106
still showed bidirectional H4/H3 reclassification (Figure 2c). Among 113 A2 H4 comparisons, 79
107
retained H4, eight changed to H3, four were model-sensitive and 22 were uninformative. Among
108
452 A2 H3 comparisons, 413 retained H3, ten changed to H4, six were model-sensitive and 23 were
109
uninformative (Figure 2d). Thus, strict matched-input transitions comprised eight H4-to-H3 and ten
110
H3-to-H4 comparisons. The 139 total A2-to-M state changes also included ambiguity and
111
information changes and cannot be interpreted as 139 corrections. Complete records are provided in
112
Source Data 1, S3/.
113
Ten of 12 historical directional transitions remained strict H4/H3 changes under matched inputs.
114
Two historical cases entered the multi-signal analysis from matched-input ambiguous states and
115
were no longer counted as strict A2-to-M reversals. Strict reversal counts therefore follow the
116
matched-input starting state. Reclassification was therefore defined by the matched-input starting
117
state; the concrete FCRL3 model contrast is developed below.

Signal sharing remained pair specific and model dependent
131
Signal-pair semantics further limited comparison-level interpretation. All 92 stable-H4 comparisons
132
and all 428 stable-H3 comparisons retained the same qualifying signal-pair identity between PF10
133
L=10 and at least one other PF10 L setting. However, 32 of the 92 H4-supported comparisons also
134
contained an H3-qualifying pair (Figure 3a). H4 support therefore meant that at least one shared pair
135
was stable, not that every signal in the region was shared. Conversely, H3 support identified a stable
136
distinct pair and did not prove the global absence of another shared pair.
137
Among the 520 comparisons with a definite PF10 H4 or H3 state, PF50 produced the same state in
138
491 (94.42%), changed four to the alternative supported state and was uninformative in 25 (Figure
139
3b). The remaining 122 PF10 model-sensitive or uninformative comparisons were not included in
140
this denominator. The 94.42% agreement is conditional on a definite PF10 state.
141
FCRL3-CD8_ET provided the clearest input-matched counterexample to a simple comparison-level
142
interpretation. Its single-causal ABF state remained H4 across A0, A1 and A2 (PP.H4=0.9413347,
143
0.9413350 and 0.9492605, respectively), whereas the PF10 multi-signal result supported H3, with
144
best PP.H4=0.0036 and PP.H3 approximately 0.992. The same comparison was H4-supported under
145
PF50 (best PP.H4=0.9919; Figure 3c). The result therefore showed that exact input matching did not
146
remove the procedure-dependent classification, while PF-number sensitivity prevented it from being
147
described as a universal CD8-cell falsification. It was evidence about the tested cell-QTL model and
148
adjustment strategy, not evidence that FCRL3 has no role in CD8 T cells.
149
FCRL3 showed stable OneK1K B-cell sharing in intermediate and memory B cells. Under PF10
150
L=10, best signal-pair PP.H4 values were 0.9937 and 0.9910, respectively. TenK10K intermediate
151
B cells reproduced the sharing pattern (343 overlapping variants; default PP.H4=0.9916; low-prior
152
H4/[H3+H4]=0.9217; Figure 5b). Because the same PBC GWAS was reused, this was cross-QTL-
153
resource support rather than independent disease replication.
154
The PBC risk allele was associated with lower FCRL3 expression in the compatible OneK1K and
155
TenK10K B-cell contexts. The frozen FinnGen public output returned no direct PBC-FCRL3 pair.
156
That non-return was a coverage boundary, not evidence against sharing. Stability within a model did
157
not establish correctness; truth-known simulations provided a complementary test.

Simulation separated shared-signal decisions from discovery adequacy
172
The primary simulation branch completed all 486,000 iterations with no recorded technical errors.
173
Multi-signal inference failed to produce an evaluable signal pair in many iterations because one or
174
both traits lacked a credible set: 130,994 iterations had no credible set for either trait, 16,819 lacked
175
a disease credible set and 177,405 lacked a QTL credible set. No iteration had credible sets for both
176
traits but no eligible pair. A total of 160,782 iterations (33.08%) were pair-evaluable (Figure 4a,d).
177
This discovery layer materially changed interpretation of unconditional performance. Pair-evaluable
178
rates ranged from 13.29% in S5 to 59.79% in S2. In S1, one true shared signal, the unconditional
179
matched H4 rate was 54.12%, whereas H4 was selected in 94.06% of pair-evaluable iterations. In
180
S4, two signals per trait with one shared pair, the corresponding rates were 9.57% and 66.72%.
181
Conditional performance showed that the estimator often recognized sharing once a signal pair
182
existed, but the unconditional rates captured the combined burden of discovery and pair
183
classification (Figure 4b).
184
Across the two frozen distinct-signal scenarios, the average false-H4 rate decreased from 12.41%
185
with ABF to 8.56% with matched multi-signal inference, a relative reduction of 31.02%. The gain
186
was not uniform. In S2, which used correlated but distinct variants, the matched false-H4 rate
187
remained 16.00% overall and 26.76% among pair-evaluable iterations. In S5, which contained two
188
high-LD signals per trait without a shared pair, the false-H4 rate fell from 4.32% with ABF to
189
1.12% with matched multi-signal inference (Figure 4c).
190
The decrease in false H4 was accompanied by lower recovery in the shared-signal scenarios:
191
average H4 recovery decreased from 32.99% with ABF to 26.66% with matched multi-signal
192
inference, a relative loss of 19.20%. This result precluded a claim of general superiority. The S6
193
mismatch sensitivity produced few decision flips in the implemented, closely related LD contrast,
194
but the zero-pair branch lacked per-trait credible-set counts. We therefore did not generalize S6 to
195
ancestry mismatch or severe reference-panel mismatch. Complete records are provided in Source
196
Data 1, S7/. LD-dependent decision rates are shown in Supplementary Figure S2.

IL12RB2 gained bounded external disease-study and chromatin support
212
IL12RB2-NK was a representative stable-H4 comparison in OneK1K. Best PF10 signal-pair PP.H4
213
values were 0.9980 across L=5, 10 and 20; PF50 L=10 yielded PP.H4=0.9965. The comparison also
214
contained a distinct signal pair, illustrating why stable H4 did not impose a single global mechanism
215
label on the region.
216
TenK10K NK-cell eQTL data reproduced the PBC-IL12RB2 sharing pattern under the bounded
217
single-causal replication model (396 overlapping variants; default PP.H4=0.9975; low-prior
218
H4/[H3+H4]=0.9760). FinnGen immune multiome outputs returned three PBC-IL12RB2
219
molecular-QTL records, for l1.NK, l1.PBMC and l2.NK strata. PP.H4 ranged from 0.9698 to
220
0.9706, with credible-set overlap of five to nine variants. These strata came from one resource and
221
were not counted as three independent cohorts.
222
The FinnGen disease signal was stable between public releases. The R12 disease credible set
223
contained 19 variants and the R13 set contained 17; all 17 R13 members occurred in R12
224
(Jaccard=0.895), the same variant led both sets, and member probabilities correlated at r=0.833
225
(Supplementary Figure S3). FinnGen R13 contained 795 PBC cases and 368,758 controls. At the
226
exact bridged disease variant rs6679356, the aligned C-allele effect was positive in both the
227
discovery PBC GWAS and FinnGen R13.
228
FinnGen R13 × OneK1K NK/IL12RB2 colocalization used 1,175 harmonized variants. PP.H4 was
229
0.9772 at p12=10^-6, 0.9977 at p12=10^-5 and 0.9998 at p12=10^-4; H4/(H3+H4) was 0.9776,
230
0.9977 and 0.9998, respectively (Figure 5a). The shared top variant was rs6702599, with concordant
231
effect direction, and both members of the OneK QTL credible set occurred in the FinnGen R13
232
disease credible set (Figure 5b). This supported the regulatory association in a different disease
233
study system. Public metadata did not establish person-level zero overlap, and the external analysis
234
remained single-causal rather than source-LD multi-signal. Complete records are provided in
235
Source Data 2, data/.
236
The prespecified CASCADE audit further constrained the chromatin interpretation. Of 27 fixed
237
genes, 22 had relevant broad-cell eQTL coverage, but only IL12RB2 returned a PBC-eQTL
238
colocalization record (Figure 5c). At the linked l1.NK peak, PBC-IL12RB2 eQTL sharing gave
239
PP.H4=0.9703 and PBC-caQTL sharing gave PP.H4=0.9695. All nine eQTL credible-set members
240
and all 11 caQTL credible-set members occurred within the 19-member disease credible set. The
241
peak was 239 bp from the IL12RB2 transcription start site and linked to the gene with coefficient
242
0.141 (Figure 5d). These three observed edges supported triangular signal coherence. They did not
243
supply the unavailable direct eQTL-caQTL posterior or establish chromatin-to-expression mediation.
244
The peak-gene link was reported with PBMC as its best cell context and did not independently
245
establish an NK-specific link.
246
The aligned PBC risk allele was associated with higher IL12RB2 expression across compatible
247
OneK1K, TenK10K and FinnGen records. Effect magnitudes were not compared because the
248
expression transformations and models differed. In the OMIX001122 processed archive, IL12RB2
249
and FCRL3 were detectable in both the single PBC and single control spatial matrices. The absence
250
of donor replication, tissue-image coordinates and spot annotations restricted this observation to
251
descriptive detectability rather than disease enrichment or spatial validation. The updated regional

Liver expression supported lineage detectability but not corrected PBC-specific enrichment
269
Both target-lineage pairs passed technical and detectability gates in all five PBC and all five control
270
liver donors. For FCRL3 in B-lineage cells, median target-lineage CPM was 5.48 in PBC and 12.45
271
in controls; the mean PBC-minus-control difference in log1p CPM was -0.786. The exact two-sided
272
permutation P value was 0.111 and the two-target BH q value was 0.111 (Figure 6a).
273
For IL12RB2 in NK-lineage cells, median target-lineage CPM was 6.66 in PBC and 4.24 in controls;
274
the mean log1p CPM difference was 0.330. The exact P value was 0.0635 and the BH q value was
275
0.111 (Figure 6b). The positive direction was descriptive and did not cross the prespecified
276
corrected threshold. Complete records are provided in Supplementary Data 1, worksheet S9; Source
277
Data 1, S9/.
278
These results established that both genes could be detected in the relevant liver immune-lineage
279
compartments in this dataset. They did not show corrected PBC-specific enrichment, tissue
280
mediation or a disease-state mechanism (Figure 6). The small donor sample and surgical non-lesion
281
controls further limited generalization. The tissue layer therefore constrained, rather than completed,
282
the regulatory narrative.

Discussion
295
This study identified three linked conditions for interpreting immune-cell regulatory assignments at
296
PBC loci: association inputs must be coordinated, the supported signal pair must be specified, and
297
stability must be separated from discovery adequacy and mechanism. Input coordination explained
298
some classification changes but left strict H4-to-H3 and H3-to-H4 transitions. Signal-pair
299
coexistence and the FCRL3 covariate-model reversal showed why a favorable gene-level label was
300
insufficient. The simulations then placed those real-data changes within a truth-known trade-off,
301
rather than treating every lower H4 count as evidence of better inference.
302
The matched-input design changes the interpretation of earlier single-causal-to-multi-signal
303
contrasts. An unmatched comparison could not distinguish the effect of a smaller variant
304
intersection from the effect of a different disease-statistic source or the effect of representing several
305
causal components [5,6,7,8]. A0/A1/A2 did not convert the final comparison into a controlled
306
experiment in which only the number of causal variants changed; ABF and SuSiE-based
307
colocalization still differ in priors, parameterization, signal discovery and decision rules. It did,
308
however, remove two concrete alternative explanations and define the residual reclassification more
309
precisely.
310
Signal-pair reporting was as important as the comparison-level count. The stability audit showed
311
that all 92 H4-supported and 428 H3-supported comparisons retained the relevant pair identity
312
across PF10 L settings. At the same time, 32 H4-supported comparisons contained a qualifying
313
distinct pair. This coexistence is biologically plausible in loci with several regulatory variants and
314
statistically incompatible with a forced one-label mechanism. The appropriate interpretation of H4
315
is that at least one disease-QTL signal pair is supported as shared under the tested model. The
316
appropriate interpretation of H3 is that a distinct pair is supported, not that the locus lacks every
317
possible shared component.
318
PF10/PF50 results provide a second boundary. Among comparisons with a definite PF10 H4/H3
319
state, 491 of 520 retained the same state under PF50. This high conditional agreement supports the
320
overall stability of many assignments. Yet FCRL3-CD8_ET showed a near-complete change from
321
H3 under PF10 to H4 under PF50. Expression-factor adjustment changes the phenotype model and
322
the residualized LD used for fine-mapping. A more favorable posterior under one specification is
323
not evidence that the specification is biologically true. The counterexample is therefore useful
324
precisely because it remains unresolved: it identifies a cell context in which regulatory attribution
325
depends on a defensible modeling choice. Because factor number changed both the QTL phenotype
326
specification and its matched LD, this contrast did not isolate an LD-only effect.
327
The simulations clarified both the benefit and the cost of the multi-signal workflow. In the frozen
328
distinct-signal scenarios, matched multi-signal inference reduced false-H4 decisions on average.
329
The improvement was largest in the high-LD two-by-two no-sharing scenario and incomplete in the
330
correlated-distinct scenario. Shared-signal recovery also decreased. This trade-off argues against
331
presenting a lower H4 count as self-validating evidence of better inference.
332
The channel audit revealed why unconditional and conditional performance differed. Two thirds of
333
the primary iterations never produced an evaluable signal pair, most often because at least one trait
334
lacked a credible set. Conditional H4 rates can be high after a pair is found while overall recovery
335

14
remains modest. These are different estimands: discovery adequacy asks whether the model
336
generates the components needed for evaluation; pair-conditional inference asks how the estimator
337
classifies an available pair. Reporting only the latter would overstate end-to-end performance,
338
whereas labeling the former as technical failure would misdescribe normal weak-signal behavior.
339
The external axes demonstrate how a reliability framework can strengthen biological interpretation
340
without inflating mechanism. IL12RB2-NK was stable across OneK1K configurations, reproduced
341
in TenK10K and supported by FinnGen molecular-QTL strata. FinnGen R13 then supported the
342
same OneK NK/IL12RB2 association in a different disease study system across the complete prior
343
series and at the source-CS level. Prior PBC studies have also prioritized IL12RB2 through
344
integrative genetic analyses [9,10], so the contribution is not first nomination of the gene. It is a
345
source-aware, cell-context-specific chain that joins multi-signal discovery evidence to bounded
346
external disease-study validation. The added chromatin layer strengthens biological coherence
347
because the disease signal shared with both the eQTL and a linked caQTL. The missing direct
348
eQTL-caQTL posterior, correlated source observations and the absence of an intervention prevent
349
this triangle from establishing causal mediation.
350
FCRL3 B-cell sharing was supported in OneK1K and TenK10K, with a consistent lower-expression
351
direction for the risk allele. Independent 2026 work has reported PBC-related FCRL3 evidence in
352
liver B cells and plasma-protein colocalization [11,12]. Those findings increase biological
353
plausibility but do not turn the present same-GWAS molecular-QTL analyses into independent
354
disease replication. The FCRL3-CD8_ET result further shows that support for one gene can be cell-
355
context specific: strong B-cell sharing can coexist with a T-cell assignment that changes under
356
covariate specification.
357
The liver analysis prevented an equally common inferential jump. Both targets were detectable in
358
the expected lineages in every donor, supporting tissue relevance at the level of presence. Neither
359
target showed corrected PBC-specific enrichment in this bounded 5-versus-5 analysis. A genotype-
360
expression association within a cell context and an average expression contrast between case and
361
control donors estimate different relationships. The latter also combines cell-state, disease-stage and
362
surgical-control differences. The null corrected result is therefore not a contradiction of the genetic
363
association, but it also cannot be used as affirmative tissue mediation.
364
The study has several strengths. It used study-derived disease LD, cell-specific active donors and
365
covariate-matched QTL LD rather than one generic reference matrix. It preserved a prespecified
366
642-comparison workload, including a large H3 layer that allowed rescue as well as falsification.
367
The matched-input audit retained the same comparison identities and did not select examples after
368
the A2-to-M results. Complete signal-pair, model-sensitivity and uninformative states were retained.
369
Finally, external QTL resources, allele direction and donor-level tissue data were assigned separate
370
evidentiary roles.
371
Several limitations define the statistical claim ceiling. Only the high-information subset received
372
multi-signal analysis, and repeated gene-cell comparisons were nested within 47 selected risk
373
regions. Neither 92/642 nor the bidirectional transition counts estimate rates across all PBC
374
comparisons. Real-data transitions have no known causal truth and therefore represent
375
reclassification, not measured error correction. Matched support and disease statistics remove two
376

15
alternative explanations, but ABF and SuSiE-based procedures still differ in discovery, priors,
377
parameterization and decision rules. The simulation used two empirical 128-variant LD templates,
378
fixed sample sizes and a finite grid; it evaluated single-configuration components rather than
379
directly calibrating the complete cross-L and low-prior gate.
380
The validation layers have distinct ceilings. OneK1K and TenK10K reused the same discovery
381
PBC GWAS. FinnGen R13 supplied a different disease study system with 795 cases, but public
382
metadata could not establish participant non-overlap, and the external analysis was single-causal
383
rather than a second source-LD multi-signal fit. The chromatin triangle lacked a direct eQTL-
384
caQTL posterior, and OMIX001122 provided one processed matrix per condition without spatial
385
coordinates. The liver analysis had five donors per group, non-lesion surgical controls and a
386
bounded target panel. Neither genetic sharing nor tissue detectability establishes that perturbing
387
IL12RB2 or FCRL3 alters a PBC-relevant phenotype.
388
Three tests would resolve distinct remaining uncertainties. First, source-matched multi-signal
389
analysis in a larger external PBC GWAS with documented participant separation would test whether
390
the same disease-QTL signal pairs persist under matched ancestry and variant support. Second, a
391
direct eQTL-caQTL analysis with common variants and source-matched LD would test whether the
392
chromatin and expression associations share a signal beyond their separate disease-sharing edges.
393
Third, perturbing IL12RB2 in NK cells and FCRL3 in B-cell subsets, with non-targeting controls,
394
would test whether altered expression changes immune activation and cholangiocyte injury in a
395
defined coculture model. Reproduced signal identity would strengthen cross-study regulatory
396
association; a perturbation response would address mechanism, and neither would alone establish
397
clinical efficacy.
398
At PBC risk loci, coordinated inputs and signal resolution changed which regulatory assignments
399
were supported, while covariate sensitivity and limited credible-set discovery constrained their
400
interpretation. External IL12RB2 evidence increased confidence in a regulatory association; FCRL3
401
exposed both reproducible B-cell sharing and a model-dependent T-cell assignment. Liver data
402
established detectability without corrected disease enrichment. Reporting these layers separately
403
makes functional prioritization more interpretable while preserving the distinction between
404
statistical sharing and mechanism.

Methods
406
Study design and governance
407
This was a secondary analysis of openly available genetic, molecular-QTL and single-cell
408
transcriptomic data. The disease, resource and analysis scope was fixed before the matched-input
409
comparison was run. Disease analysis used the European PBC meta-analysis and 56 non-HLA
410
regional definitions. The molecular layer used 14 OneK1K immune-cell types. The initial registry
411
contained 6,923 locus-gene-cell comparisons. Multi-signal analysis was restricted to a frozen 642-
412
comparison high-information subset rather than extended to all screened comparisons.
413
The 642 comparisons retained their prespecified roles: 184 formed the primary ABF trigger-
414
verification cohort, 455 formed a symmetric H3 rescue/falsification layer, and three were borderline
415
high-information calibration cases. These identities were not changed after observing multi-signal
416

16
or matched-input results. The matched-input A0/A1/A2 analysis was a result-informed
417
methodological audit developed to resolve a documented input-asymmetry problem; it was not
418
described as an external preregistration. No locus, gene or cell type was added in response to its
419
outputs.
420
The analysis comprised source validation, harmonization, ABF screening, high-information follow-
421
up, cell-specific LD construction, multi-signal inference, diagnostic review, matched-input
422
comparison, simulations and bounded external and tissue evaluation. The liver analysis preceded the
423
PBC-wide design; signal-semantics and matched-input comparisons were post-result audits.
424
Negative, model-sensitive, coverage-limited and uninformative results were retained.
425
PBC association data and study-derived disease LD
426
PBC summary statistics were obtained from GWAS Catalog study GCST90061440, representing
427
the GRCh37 European five-panel meta-analysis reported by Cordell and colleagues [2]
428
(https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/studies/GCST90061440). The dataset comprised 8,021 cases and
429
16,489 controls (total N=24,510). After byte-level and schema validation, 5,054,572 rows contained
430
valid numeric association data. Study-derived regional association summaries and LD matrices were
431
obtained from the public GJOKA archive accompanying the PBC fine-mapping analysis [13]
432
(https://www.staff.ncl.ac.uk/heather.cordell/GjokaPaper.html).
433
The GJOKA resource defined 56 non-HLA regions. Disease-side multi-signal analysis used each
434
region's aligned summary z statistics and study-derived LD after intersection with the comparison-
435
specific QTL input. The regional files, row order, alleles and matrices were tied to stored
436
checksums. We did not substitute a generic external LD reference for the primary disease analysis.
437
OneK1K expression-QTL data and PBC-wide comparison registry
438
The cohort origin was the OneK1K single-cell peripheral-blood study [3]. The present reanalysis
439
used the updated 980-donor genotype, covariate and expression resource associated with Xue et al.
440
and Zenodo record 18910121 [14,15]. The cohort publication and the exact analysis release
441
therefore have distinct provenance roles. We retained the 14 source cell labels used by the frozen
442
workflow. Gene eligibility and locus assignment were inherited from the pre-result manifest: genes
443
were assigned to a disease region when the gene transcription start site fell within the region
444
extended by 1 Mb and the gene met the source-level eGene rule (q<0.05) in at least one cell type.
445
Once a gene entered the registry, available source top-summary records across the retained cells
446
were preserved rather than restricted to cells with the smallest q value.
447
This procedure yielded 6,923 locus-gene-cell comparisons. Of these, 5,460 had at least 200 aligned
448
variants and were eligible for the ABF screen; 1,463 had insufficient overlap and were retained as
449
technical indeterminates rather than biological negatives. The eligible universe contained repeated
450
cells and genes within loci, so comparisons were not treated as independent discoveries.
451
Variant identity, allele alignment and exact support sets
452
Variants were represented by chromosome, GRCh37 position and alleles. For ABF calculations and
453
cross-resource effect-direction comparisons, disease and QTL effects were aligned to the OneK1K
454
PLINK BIM A1 allele. In the GJOKA multi-signal input, disease z statistics remained in the
455

17
GJOKA effect-allele orientation paired with the corresponding disease LD; QTL z statistics
456
remained paired with BIM-A1 QTL LD. Variant identities and ordering were matched across traits,
457
whereas each trait retained internally consistent effect and LD signs. Strand complements were
458
allowed only when allele identity remained unambiguous. Palindromic variants were excluded when
459
source metadata and allele frequency did not resolve orientation. Duplicated or conflicting identities,
460
nonnumeric effects or standard errors, and variants absent from the relevant LD matrix were
461
removed before posterior calculation.
462
Two comparison-specific support sets were distinguished. S_A was the variant support used by the
463
historical ABF screen. S_M was the actual intersection used by the multi-signal analysis after
464
disease, QTL and LD alignment. Across the frozen 642 comparisons, S_M contained 19-114 fewer
465
variants than S_A (median 65; median reduction 7.67%). Exact member identities and row order,
466
rather than variant counts alone, defined equality.
467
Historical single-causal ABF screen
468
Single-causal colocalization followed the approximate Bayes factor framework of Giambartolomei
469
et al. [5]. Case-control disease effects used a prior standard deviation of 0.20. Quantitative-trait
470
QTL effects used 0.15 multiplied by the estimated phenotype standard deviation (sdY). Priors were
471
p1=1x10^-4, p2=1x10^-4 and p12=1x10^-5, with p12=1x10^-6 and 1x10^-4 retained for sensitivity
472
analysis. The primary posterior quantities were PP.H3, representing distinct associated variants,
473
PP.H4, representing one shared associated variant, and H4/(H3+H4), conditioning on the distinct-
474
versus-shared alternatives.
475
A default-prior H4 screening trigger required PP.H4>=0.80 and H4/(H3+H4)>=0.80. The lower and
476
higher p12 results were retained as sensitivity outputs, not as additional admission conditions.
477
Among comparisons that did not meet the H4 rule, H3/H4 ambiguity required H3+H4>=0.80 and
478
0.20<=H4/(H3+H4)<=0.80; high-information H3 required H3+H4>=0.80 and H4/(H3+H4)<0.20.
479
The expanded 642-comparison workload retained the high-information H3/H4 subset, including the
480
three borderline cases. These screening rules did not establish final multi-signal support.
481
Source-matched QTL LD and current-release model identity
482
For each OneK1K cell-locus block, genotype dosage was extracted only for donors active in that
483
cell type. A global genotype cohort was not substituted for cell types with smaller active-donor sets.
484
Genotypes were aligned to the expression-QTL effect allele. Raw genotype correlations were
485
retained for diagnostics. Model-matched QTL LD was calculated after projecting the genotype
486
dosage matrix G off the same covariate design C used in the corresponding QTL analysis:
487
G* = [I - C(C^T C)^-1 C^T]G,
488
and R_QTL = cor(G*).
489
The covariate design included sex, age, six genotype principal components and expression factors.
490
PF10, using ten expression factors, was the primary specification; PF50, using 50 factors, was a
491
prespecified sensitivity model. Current-release PF10 and PF50 QTL summaries and LD were
492
generated from matched phenotype, genotype, active-donor and covariate sources. The earlier
493
targeted dual-model gate evaluated 14 comparison-model identity rows from seven frozen
494

18
comparisons; this count must not be read as 14 independently validated cell types. The expanded
495
study retained 14 cell labels and comparison-specific source manifests. Matrix dimension, variant
496
order, symmetry, diagonal, finite values, rank behavior and positive-semidefinite tolerance were
497
checked before fine-mapping.
498
Multi-signal fine-mapping and signal-pair colocalization
499
Disease and QTL association summaries were fine-mapped with SuSiE-RSS [8], the summary-data
500
extension of the SuSiE model [6]. The primary PF10 model was evaluated at L=5, 10 and 20; PF50
501
was evaluated at L=10. Fits used estimate_residual_variance=FALSE,
502
estimate_prior_variance=TRUE, max_iter=2000, tol=1x10^-4, 95% credible sets and minimum
503
absolute within-set correlation of 0.5. Disease sample size was 24,510; QTL sample sizes followed
504
the cell-specific donor counts.
505
Signal-pair colocalization used coloc.susie [7]. All eligible disease-QTL credible-set pairs were
506
evaluated using the same p12 sensitivity series as the ABF screen. For a given configuration, an H4-
507
qualifying pair required default PP.H4>=0.80, default H4/(H3+H4)>=0.80 and H4/(H3+H4)>=0.50
508
at p12=1x10^-6 for that same pair. An H3-qualifying pair required default PP.H3>=0.80 and
509
H4/(H3+H4)<=0.20. A stable PF10 comparison required the relevant L=10 support and support in
510
at least one of L=5 or L=20. H4 was assigned before H3 when both were available. Comparisons
511
without stable H4/H3 support but with a high-information pair in any required PF10 configuration
512
were model-sensitive; the remainder were uninformative. The subsequent signal-identity audit
513
added cross-L correspondence without overwriting these historical labels.
514
In the post-result signal-semantics audit, signal identity was matched across L settings using exact
515
lead-pair identity or a credible-set Jaccard overlap of at least 0.50 for both traits. H4 and H3 pairs
516
were recorded separately. A comparison could therefore support at least one shared pair and still
517
contain a different H3-qualifying pair. Bayesian posterior thresholds were not interpreted as family-
518
wise error or false-discovery-rate control across the correlated comparison universe.
519
Multi-signal diagnostic adjudication
520
Corrected kriging diagnostics were evaluated for every comparison-model-trait unit: 642
521
comparisons x two QTL covariate models x two traits, for 2,568 units. Returned key structure,
522
expected and observed row counts and finite values were checked. Both the historical logLR>2
523
count and the source-code plotting flag (logLR>2 and abs(z)>2) were retained. All 2,568 diagnostic
524
units were evaluated and passed the recorded review gate; a reviewed flag was not recoded as no
525
anomaly. One unique official-rule event, rs1800378, was reviewed; it did not enter a disease or QTL
526
credible set and did not trigger a refit. This diagnostic repair occurred after the original multi-signal
527
run and was disclosed as a post-result audit.

Matched-input A0/A1/A2/M attribution design
529
We constructed four analysis arms for the frozen 642 comparisons. A0 replayed the historical ABF
530
calculation using the original harmonized GCST disease statistics and S_A. A1 retained those
531
disease statistics but restricted both traits to S_M, isolating the effect of support-set restriction at the
532
categorical level. A2 retained S_M and used the GJOKA matched-z disease definition aligned to the
533

19
disease LD source. M was the already frozen PF10 multi-signal outcome and was not refitted for
534
this comparison.
535
A0 replay reproduced the historical posteriors to a maximum absolute difference of 3.55x10^-13.
536
Fixed sdY was used for the primary A1 and A2 contrasts so support-set differences did not also alter
537
the QTL effect scale. Native-sdY sensitivity analyses were reported separately. GJOKA matched-z
538
statistics were primary for A2; an analysis based on the rounded public beta and standard error was
539
retained as a statistic-definition sensitivity analysis.
540
We counted all adjacent categorical changes for A0-to-A1, A1-to-A2 and A2-to-M, but did not add
541
those counts because the affected comparisons could overlap. Strict bidirectional reclassification
542
was reserved for H4-to-H3 and H3-to-H4 changes between A2 and M. Other transitions to or from
543
ambiguous, model-sensitive or uninformative states were retained as uncertainty changes. Because
544
A2 and M are complete inferential procedures with different assumptions and parameterizations,
545
A2-to-M was not described as a single-factor experiment or as a truth-known correction rate.

Simulation design and outcome channels
547
The frozen simulation contained 486 parameter combinations with 1,000 iterations each, for
548
486,000 primary matched-LD iterations. Summary z statistics were generated with two empirical
549
128-variant LD templates. Six scenarios were evaluated: one shared signal (S1); correlated but
550
distinct signals (S2); two disease signals and one QTL signal with partial sharing (S3); two signals
551
per trait with one shared pair (S4); two signals per trait with no shared pair under high LD (S5); and
552
a matched-versus-mismatched LD sensitivity scenario (S6). Disease N=24,510 and QTL N=750
553
were fixed, not varied. The 486 grid rows were six scenarios crossed with three MAF values (0.05,
554
0.20, 0.40), three target causal-pair r-squared values (0.20, 0.50, 0.80), three L values (5, 10, 20)
555
and three p12 values (1x10^-6, 1x10^-5, 1x10^-4). Each row allocated 500 iterations to each
556
empirical template.
557
The two templates used disease/QTL LD from locus 2/NK and locus 4/B_IN. Simulated summaries
558
followed z ~ Normal(sqrt(N) R b_std, R), with per-allele effects scaled by sqrt(2 MAF(1-MAF));
559
the first disease effect was log(1.12), the first QTL effect was 0.30, and second effects were -0.8
560
times the first. These were summary-z experiments rather than individual-level binary PBC
561
simulations. S6 changed only the analysis QTL LD from the same-locus PF10 to PF50 matrix,
562
preserving trait identities and variant order.
563
Each simulated comparison was evaluated at one L and one p12. Thus, this component-level
564
experiment did not directly calibrate the real-data composite gate that also required cross-L stability
565
and same-pair low-prior support. Scenario-level rates averaged the frozen MAF, LD, L and prior
566
grid; they were not error rates at a single default-prior operating point.
567
ABF and matched multi-signal decisions were recorded for every iteration. The multi-signal branch
568
additionally classified each iteration into both traits lacking a credible set, disease-only absence,
569
QTL-only absence, both traits having credible sets but no evaluable pair, an H3 pair, an H4 pair, or
570
a pair-evaluable uninformative result. Technical errors were counted separately. Unconditional
571
decision rates used all iterations; pair-conditional rates used only iterations with an evaluable signal
572

20
pair. The latter describe estimator behavior after the discovery stage and were not directly compared
573
with the ABF unconditional denominator as if they were the same estimand.

outputs of the population-scale immune multiome resource [17] for the two representative genes.

genes and their corresponding broad cell strata. For those genes, we recorded relevant-cell eQTL

availability and returned PBC-eQTL colocalization. The IL12RB2-linked peak chr1-67307618-

Donor-level liver target-panel analysis
623
HRA008003 is an open-access single-cell study of liver and blood in PBC [19]
624
(https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/gsa-human/browse/HRA008003). We analyzed liver BAM files from five
625
treatment-naive PBC donors (HRR1849459-HRR1849463) and five non-lesion liver controls
626
obtained during hepatic hemangioma surgery (HRR1849454-HRR1849458). Source sizes and
627
checksums were verified, and each BAM passed samtools quickcheck and tag-schema preflight.

629
barcode and a unique gene assignment; unmapped, secondary and supplementary alignments were
630
excluded. Cell calling used the library-specific order-of-magnitude rule with an expected recovered-
631
cell count of 6,000: the UMI threshold was the ceiling of one tenth of the 99th-percentile count
632
among the 6,000 highest-count barcodes. Called-cell counts had to fall between 2,500 and 7,500,
633
with median total UMI count at least 500. B markers were CD79A, CD79B, MS4A1, CD37, CD74,
634

637
genes and three panel UMIs. B-panel UMIs had to exceed NK, T and myeloid panel counts; NK-
638
panel UMIs had to exceed B and myeloid counts and be at least the T-panel count. Each donor-
639
lineage unit required at least ten cells. Target detectability required at least three target UMIs and
640

641
multiplied by 10^6.

643
prespecified lineage. Group differences were compared with the exact distribution of all 252

assignments of five of ten donors to the PBC label. Two-sided exact P values were adjusted across
645
the two target-lineage pairs using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Cell-level observations were

not used as independent case-control replicates. The controls were non-lesion surgical liver samples,

not healthy volunteer livers.

Abstract
10
Regulatory assignments depend on association inputs and signal models. We screened 5,460 of
11
6,923 primary biliary cholangitis locus-gene-cell comparisons and evaluated a protocol-frozen 642-
12
comparison subset. Matching variant support and disease statistics changed 15 and 19 classifications,
13
respectively. Eight shared-signal (H4) calls became distinct-signal (H3), and ten changed conversely.
14
Shared and distinct pairs coexisted in 32 of 92 H4-supported comparisons, while a FCRL3 T-cell
15
assignment reversed between covariate models. Across 486,000 simulations, multi-signal inference
16
reduced false sharing from 12.41% to 8.56% and shared-signal recovery from 32.99% to 26.66%;
17
only 33.08% were pair-evaluable. IL12RB2 sharing in natural killer cells received external disease-
18
study and chromatin support, whereas liver data showed detectability without corrected disease
19
enrichment. These results support signal-specific, model-qualified regulatory attribution without
20
establishing mediation or universal methodological superiority.
21
Keywords: primary biliary cholangitis; colocalization; single-cell eQTL; fine-mapping; linkage
22
disequilibrium; signal pair; regulatory genomics; statistical genetics
23
Introduction
24
Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is an autoimmune cholestatic liver disease characterized by
25
progressive injury to small intrahepatic bile ducts [1]. Genome-wide association studies have
26
identified a substantial inherited component and many non-HLA susceptibility loci, creating a
27
strong foundation for mechanistic prioritization [2]. The central interpretive problem is no longer
28
whether associated regions exist. It is whether a regional disease association and a molecular
29
quantitative-trait locus (QTL) implicate the same local signal, in which gene and cellular context,
30
and with what degree of uncertainty. Functional follow-up depends on resolving that uncertainty: a
31
strongly associated gene in the wrong cell context can direct experiments toward a regulatory
32
assignment that the genetic data do not support.
33
Single-cell QTL resources make this problem biologically more specific. OneK1K mapped cell-
34
type-specific genetic effects on gene expression in peripheral blood immune populations [3], and
35
TenK10K extends immune-cell molecular-QTL mapping to a larger donor cohort and a broader
36
cellular taxonomy [4]. These resources allow the same disease locus to be compared across genes
37
and cell contexts. That resolution also increases statistical dependence: a locus can contain several
38

2
disease and expression signals, the same gene can appear in related immune populations, and a
39
comparison-level label can conceal different signal pairs.
40
Approximate Bayes factor (ABF) colocalization provides an efficient first-pass test of whether two
41
association patterns are more compatible with one shared causal variant (H4) or with two distinct
42
causal variants (H3) [5]. Its standard formulation assumes at most one causal variant per trait in the
43
tested region. That assumption can be restrictive in autoimmune loci with allelic heterogeneity.
44
Multi-signal fine-mapping and signal-pair colocalization can instead represent several local
45
components [6,7], but a direct comparison is difficult when the procedures use different variant sets,
46
disease summaries or linkage disequilibrium (LD) inputs. An apparent H4-to-H3 or H3-to-H4
47
change can then reflect input mismatch as well as inferential structure.
48
This distinction matters for biological attribution. A stable shared signal pair supports a locus-gene-
49
cell regulatory association, but it does not prove expression mediation or a molecular mechanism. A
50
stable distinct pair does not imply that the entire locus contains no shared signal. Indeed, shared and
51
distinct signal pairs can coexist within one locus-gene-cell comparison. Model sensitivity can also
52
be informative: it identifies assignments that depend on the covariate adjustment used to construct
53
QTL summaries and model-matched LD, rather than providing a reason to select the configuration
54
that yields the most favorable posterior.
55
We used PBC to test the reliability of immune-cell regulatory attribution through a linked sequence
56
of questions. A PBC-wide screen defined a bounded high-information subset. Matched-input single-
57
causal arms then distinguished changes caused by variant support and disease-statistic definitions
58
from differences remaining between complete inferential procedures. Signal-pair identity and
59
covariate sensitivity established what a comparison-level label could mean. Truth-known
60
simulations tested the trade-off between false sharing, recovery and credible-set discovery. Finally,
61
representative FCRL3 B-cell and IL12RB2-NK assignments were examined across molecular-QTL
62
resources, a different disease study system, linked chromatin and donor-level liver expression. This
63
design asked which assignments persisted, why others changed, and where statistical support
64
stopped short of mechanism.
65
Results
66
PBC-wide screening defined a bounded high-information multi-signal analysis
67
The frozen registry contained 6,923 locus-gene-cell comparisons. Of these, 5,460 met the overlap
68
threshold for ABF screening and 1,463 were coverage-insufficient (Figure 1a). The latter were not
69
interpreted as negative colocalization results. The multi-signal workload contained 642 comparisons:
70
184 primary trigger-verification comparisons, 455 H3 rescue/falsification comparisons and three
71
borderline calibration cases (Figure 1d). It covered 47 PBC regions, 200 genes, 14 cell types and
72
286 cell-locus blocks. Complete records are provided in Source Data 1, S2/. The four-arm input
73
contract is shown in Figure 1b; the complete adjacent transition matrices are provided in
74
Supplementary Figure S1.
75
The final PF10 multi-signal classification contained 92 H4-supported comparisons, 428 H3-
76
supported comparisons, 59 model-sensitive comparisons and 63 uninformative comparisons (Figure
77
1c). These are comparison counts, not independent genes or loci. The 92 H4-supported comparisons

Signal sharing remained pair specific and model dependent
107

108

110

111

112
distinct pair and did not prove the global absence of another shared pair.

135

136

137

138

139

141

Discussion
219
This study identified three linked conditions for interpreting immune-cell regulatory assignments at
220
PBC loci: association inputs must be coordinated, the supported signal pair must be specified, and
221
stability must be separated from discovery adequacy and mechanism. Input coordination explained
222
some classification changes but left strict H4-to-H3 and H3-to-H4 transitions. Signal-pair
223
coexistence and the FCRL3 covariate-model reversal showed why a favorable gene-level label was
224
insufficient. The simulations then placed those real-data changes within a truth-known trade-off,
225
rather than treating every lower H4 count as evidence of better inference.
226
The matched-input design changes the interpretation of earlier single-causal-to-multi-signal
227
contrasts. An unmatched comparison could not distinguish the effect of a smaller variant
228
intersection from the effect of a different disease-statistic source or the effect of representing several
229
causal components [5,6,7,8]. A0/A1/A2 did not convert the final comparison into a controlled
230
experiment in which only the number of causal variants changed; ABF and SuSiE-based
231
colocalization still differ in priors, parameterization, signal discovery and decision rules. It did,
232
however, remove two concrete alternative explanations and define the residual reclassification more
233
precisely.
234
Signal-pair reporting was as important as the comparison-level count. The stability audit showed
235
that all 92 H4-supported and 428 H3-supported comparisons retained the relevant pair identity
236
across PF10 L settings. At the same time, 32 H4-supported comparisons contained a qualifying
237

7
distinct pair. This coexistence is biologically plausible in loci with several regulatory variants and
238
statistically incompatible with a forced one-label mechanism. The appropriate interpretation of H4
239
is that at least one disease-QTL signal pair is supported as shared under the tested model. The
240
appropriate interpretation of H3 is that a distinct pair is supported, not that the locus lacks every
241
possible shared component.
242
PF10/PF50 results provide a second boundary. Among comparisons with a definite PF10 H4/H3
243
state, 491 of 520 retained the same state under PF50. This high conditional agreement supports the
244
overall stability of many assignments. Yet FCRL3-CD8_ET showed a near-complete change from
245
H3 under PF10 to H4 under PF50. Expression-factor adjustment changes the phenotype model and
246
the residualized LD used for fine-mapping. A more favorable posterior under one specification is
247
not evidence that the specification is biologically true. The counterexample is therefore useful
248
precisely because it remains unresolved: it identifies a cell context in which regulatory attribution
249
depends on a defensible modeling choice. Because factor number changed both the QTL phenotype
250
specification and its matched LD, this contrast did not isolate an LD-only effect.
251
The simulations clarified both the benefit and the cost of the multi-signal workflow. In the frozen
252
distinct-signal scenarios, matched multi-signal inference reduced false-H4 decisions on average.
253
The improvement was largest in the high-LD two-by-two no-sharing scenario and incomplete in the
254
correlated-distinct scenario. Shared-signal recovery also decreased. This trade-off argues against
255
presenting a lower H4 count as self-validating evidence of better inference.
256
The channel audit revealed why unconditional and conditional performance differed. Two thirds of
257
the primary iterations never produced an evaluable signal pair, most often because at least one trait
258
lacked a credible set. Conditional H4 rates can be high after a pair is found while overall recovery
259
remains modest. These are different estimands: discovery adequacy asks whether the model
260
generates the components needed for evaluation; pair-conditional inference asks how the estimator
261
classifies an available pair. Reporting only the latter would overstate end-to-end performance,
262
whereas labeling the former as technical failure would misdescribe normal weak-signal behavior.
263
The external axes demonstrate how a reliability framework can strengthen biological interpretation
264
without inflating mechanism. IL12RB2-NK was stable across OneK1K configurations, reproduced
265
in TenK10K and supported by FinnGen molecular-QTL strata. FinnGen R13 then supported the
266
same OneK NK/IL12RB2 association in a different disease study system across the complete prior
267
series and at the source-CS level. Prior PBC studies have also prioritized IL12RB2 through
268
integrative genetic analyses [9,10], so the contribution is not first nomination of the gene. It is a
269
source-aware, cell-context-specific chain that joins multi-signal discovery evidence to bounded
270
external disease-study validation. The added chromatin layer strengthens biological coherence
271
because the disease signal shared with both the eQTL and a linked caQTL. The missing direct
272
eQTL-caQTL posterior, correlated source observations and the absence of an intervention prevent
273
this triangle from establishing causal mediation.
274
FCRL3 B-cell sharing was supported in OneK1K and TenK10K, with a consistent lower-expression
275
direction for the risk allele. Independent 2026 work has reported PBC-related FCRL3 evidence in
276
liver B cells and plasma-protein colocalization [11,12]. Those findings increase biological
277
plausibility but do not turn the present same-GWAS molecular-QTL analyses into independent
278

8
disease replication. The FCRL3-CD8_ET result further shows that support for one gene can be cell-
279
context specific: strong B-cell sharing can coexist with a T-cell assignment that changes under
280
covariate specification.
281
The liver analysis prevented an equally common inferential jump. Both targets were detectable in
282
the expected lineages in every donor, supporting tissue relevance at the level of presence. Neither
283
target showed corrected PBC-specific enrichment in this bounded 5-versus-5 analysis. A genotype-
284
expression association within a cell context and an average expression contrast between case and
285
control donors estimate different relationships. The latter also combines cell-state, disease-stage and
286
surgical-control differences. The null corrected result is therefore not a contradiction of the genetic
287
association, but it also cannot be used as affirmative tissue mediation.
288
The study has several strengths. It used study-derived disease LD, cell-specific active donors and
289
covariate-matched QTL LD rather than one generic reference matrix. It preserved a prespecified
290
642-comparison workload, including a large H3 layer that allowed rescue as well as falsification.
291
The matched-input audit retained the same comparison identities and did not select examples after
292
the A2-to-M results. Complete signal-pair, model-sensitivity and uninformative states were retained.
293
Finally, external QTL resources, allele direction and donor-level tissue data were assigned separate
294
evidentiary roles.
295
Several limitations define the statistical claim ceiling. Only the high-information subset received
296
multi-signal analysis, and repeated gene-cell comparisons were nested within 47 selected risk
297
regions. Neither 92/642 nor the bidirectional transition counts estimate rates across all PBC
298
comparisons. Real-data transitions have no known causal truth and therefore represent
299
reclassification, not measured error correction. Matched support and disease statistics remove two
300
alternative explanations, but ABF and SuSiE-based procedures still differ in discovery, priors,
301
parameterization and decision rules. The simulation used two empirical 128-variant LD templates,
302
fixed sample sizes and a finite grid; it evaluated single-configuration components rather than
303
directly calibrating the complete cross-L and low-prior gate.
304
The validation layers have distinct ceilings. OneK1K and TenK10K reused the same discovery
305
PBC GWAS. FinnGen R13 supplied a different disease study system with 795 cases, but public
306
metadata could not establish participant non-overlap, and the external analysis was single-causal
307
rather than a second source-LD multi-signal fit. The chromatin triangle lacked a direct eQTL-
308
caQTL posterior, and OMIX001122 provided one processed matrix per condition without spatial
309
coordinates. The liver analysis had five donors per group, non-lesion surgical controls and a
310
bounded target panel. Neither genetic sharing nor tissue detectability establishes that perturbing
311
IL12RB2 or FCRL3 alters a PBC-relevant phenotype.
312
Three tests would resolve distinct remaining uncertainties. First, source-matched multi-signal
313
analysis in a larger external PBC GWAS with documented participant separation would test whether
314
the same disease-QTL signal pairs persist under matched ancestry and variant support. Second, a
315
direct eQTL-caQTL analysis with common variants and source-matched LD would test whether the
316
chromatin and expression associations share a signal beyond their separate disease-sharing edges.
317
Third, perturbing IL12RB2 in NK cells and FCRL3 in B-cell subsets, with non-targeting controls,
318
would test whether altered expression changes immune activation and cholangiocyte injury in a
319

9
defined coculture model. Reproduced signal identity would strengthen cross-study regulatory
320
association; a perturbation response would address mechanism, and neither would alone establish
321
clinical efficacy.
322
At PBC risk loci, coordinated inputs and signal resolution changed which regulatory assignments
323
were supported, while covariate sensitivity and limited credible-set discovery constrained their
324
interpretation. External IL12RB2 evidence increased confidence in a regulatory association; FCRL3
325
exposed both reproducible B-cell sharing and a model-dependent T-cell assignment. Liver data
326
established detectability without corrected disease enrichment. Reporting these layers separately
327
makes functional prioritization more interpretable while preserving the distinction between
328
statistical sharing and mechanism.

Methods
330
Study design and governance
331
This was a secondary analysis of openly available genetic, molecular-QTL and single-cell
332
transcriptomic data. The disease, resource and analysis scope was fixed before the matched-input
333
comparison was run. Disease analysis used the European PBC meta-analysis and 56 non-HLA
334
regional definitions. The molecular layer used 14 OneK1K immune-cell types. The initial registry
335
contained 6,923 locus-gene-cell comparisons. Multi-signal analysis was restricted to a frozen 642-
336
comparison high-information subset rather than extended to all screened comparisons.
337
The 642 comparisons retained their prespecified roles: 184 formed the primary ABF trigger-
338
verification cohort, 455 formed a symmetric H3 rescue/falsification layer, and three were borderline
339
high-information calibration cases. These identities were not changed after observing multi-signal
340
or matched-input results. The matched-input A0/A1/A2 analysis was a result-informed
341
methodological audit developed to resolve a documented input-asymmetry problem; it was not
342
described as an external preregistration. No locus, gene or cell type was added in response to its
343
outputs.
344
The analysis comprised source validation, harmonization, ABF screening, high-information follow-
345
up, cell-specific LD construction, multi-signal inference, diagnostic review, matched-input
346
comparison, simulations and bounded external and tissue evaluation. The liver analysis preceded the
347
PBC-wide design; signal-semantics and matched-input comparisons were post-result audits.
348
Negative, model-sensitive, coverage-limited and uninformative results were retained.
349

350
PBC summary statistics were obtained from GWAS Catalog study GCST90061440, representing
351
the GRCh37 European five-panel meta-analysis reported by Cordell and colleagues [2]
352
(https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/studies/GCST90061440). The dataset comprised 8,021 cases and
353
16,489 controls (total N=24,510). After byte-level and schema validation, 5,054,572 rows contained
354
valid numeric association data. Study-derived regional association summaries and LD matrices were
355
obtained from the public GJOKA archive accompanying the PBC fine-mapping analysis [13]
356
(https://www.staff.ncl.ac.uk/heather.cordell/GjokaPaper.html).
357

10
The GJOKA resource defined 56 non-HLA regions. Disease-side multi-signal analysis used each
358
region's aligned summary z statistics and study-derived LD after intersection with the comparison-
359
specific QTL input. The regional files, row order, alleles and matrices were tied to stored
360
checksums. We did not substitute a generic external LD reference for the primary disease analysis.
361
OneK1K expression-QTL data and PBC-wide comparison registry
362
The cohort origin was the OneK1K single-cell peripheral-blood study [3]. The present reanalysis
363
used the updated 980-donor genotype, covariate and expression resource associated with Xue et al.
364
and Zenodo record 18910121 [14,15]. The cohort publication and the exact analysis release
365
therefore have distinct provenance roles. We retained the 14 source cell labels used by the frozen
366
workflow. Gene eligibility and locus assignment were inherited from the pre-result manifest: genes
367
were assigned to a disease region when the gene transcription start site fell within the region
368
extended by 1 Mb and the gene met the source-level eGene rule (q<0.05) in at least one cell type.
369
Once a gene entered the registry, available source top-summary records across the retained cells
370
were preserved rather than restricted to cells with the smallest q value.
371
This procedure yielded 6,923 locus-gene-cell comparisons. Of these, 5,460 had at least 200 aligned
372
variants and were eligible for the ABF screen; 1,463 had insufficient overlap and were retained as
373
technical indeterminates rather than biological negatives. The eligible universe contained repeated
374
cells and genes within loci, so comparisons were not treated as independent discoveries.
375
Variant identity, allele alignment and exact support sets
376
Variants were represented by chromosome, GRCh37 position and alleles. For ABF calculations and
377
cross-resource effect-direction comparisons, disease and QTL effects were aligned to the OneK1K
378
PLINK BIM A1 allele. In the GJOKA multi-signal input, disease z statistics remained in the
379
GJOKA effect-allele orientation paired with the corresponding disease LD; QTL z statistics
380
remained paired with BIM-A1 QTL LD. Variant identities and ordering were matched across traits,
381
whereas each trait retained internally consistent effect and LD signs. Strand complements were
382
allowed only when allele identity remained unambiguous. Palindromic variants were excluded when
383
source metadata and allele frequency did not resolve orientation. Duplicated or conflicting identities,
384
nonnumeric effects or standard errors, and variants absent from the relevant LD matrix were
385
removed before posterior calculation.
386
Two comparison-specific support sets were distinguished. S_A was the variant support used by the
387
historical ABF screen. S_M was the actual intersection used by the multi-signal analysis after
388
disease, QTL and LD alignment. Across the frozen 642 comparisons, S_M contained 19-114 fewer
389
variants than S_A (median 65; median reduction 7.67%). Exact member identities and row order,
390
rather than variant counts alone, defined equality.
391
Historical single-causal ABF screen
392
Single-causal colocalization followed the approximate Bayes factor framework of Giambartolomei
393
et al. [5]. Case-control disease effects used a prior standard deviation of 0.20. Quantitative-trait
394
QTL effects used 0.15 multiplied by the estimated phenotype standard deviation (sdY). Priors were
395
p1=1x10^-4, p2=1x10^-4 and p12=1x10^-5, with p12=1x10^-6 and 1x10^-4 retained for sensitivity
396

11
analysis. The primary posterior quantities were PP.H3, representing distinct associated variants,
397
PP.H4, representing one shared associated variant, and H4/(H3+H4), conditioning on the distinct-
398
versus-shared alternatives.
399
A default-prior H4 screening trigger required PP.H4>=0.80 and H4/(H3+H4)>=0.80. The lower and
400
higher p12 results were retained as sensitivity outputs, not as additional admission conditions.
401
Among comparisons that did not meet the H4 rule, H3/H4 ambiguity required H3+H4>=0.80 and
402
0.20<=H4/(H3+H4)<=0.80; high-information H3 required H3+H4>=0.80 and H4/(H3+H4)<0.20.
403
The expanded 642-comparison workload retained the high-information H3/H4 subset, including the
404
three borderline cases. These screening rules did not establish final multi-signal support.
405
Source-matched QTL LD and current-release model identity
406
For each OneK1K cell-locus block, genotype dosage was extracted only for donors active in that
407
cell type. A global genotype cohort was not substituted for cell types with smaller active-donor sets.
408
Genotypes were aligned to the expression-QTL effect allele. Raw genotype correlations were
409
retained for diagnostics. Model-matched QTL LD was calculated after projecting the genotype
410
dosage matrix G off the same covariate design C used in the corresponding QTL analysis:
411
G* = [I - C(C^T C)^-1 C^T]G,
412
and R_QTL = cor(G*).
413
The covariate design included sex, age, six genotype principal components and expression factors.
414
PF10, using ten expression factors, was the primary specification; PF50, using 50 factors, was a
415
prespecified sensitivity model. Current-release PF10 and PF50 QTL summaries and LD were
416
generated from matched phenotype, genotype, active-donor and covariate sources. The earlier
417
targeted dual-model gate evaluated 14 comparison-model identity rows from seven frozen
418
comparisons; this count must not be read as 14 independently validated cell types. The expanded
419
study retained 14 cell labels and comparison-specific source manifests. Matrix dimension, variant
420
order, symmetry, diagonal, finite values, rank behavior and positive-semidefinite tolerance were
421
checked before fine-mapping.

Multi-signal fine-mapping and signal-pair colocalization
423
Disease and QTL association summaries were fine-mapped with SuSiE-RSS [8], the summary-data
424
extension of the SuSiE model [6]. The primary PF10 model was evaluated at L=5, 10 and 20; PF50
425
was evaluated at L=10. Fits used estimate_residual_variance=FALSE,
426
estimate_prior_variance=TRUE, max_iter=2000, tol=1x10^-4, 95% credible sets and minimum
427
absolute within-set correlation of 0.5. Disease sample size was 24,510; QTL sample sizes followed
428
the cell-specific donor counts.
429
Signal-pair colocalization used coloc.susie [7]. All eligible disease-QTL credible-set pairs were
430
evaluated using the same p12 sensitivity series as the ABF screen. For a given configuration, an H4-
431
qualifying pair required default PP.H4>=0.80, default H4/(H3+H4)>=0.80 and H4/(H3+H4)>=0.50
432
at p12=1x10^-6 for that same pair. An H3-qualifying pair required default PP.H3>=0.80 and
433
H4/(H3+H4)<=0.20. A stable PF10 comparison required the relevant L=10 support and support in
434
at least one of L=5 or L=20. H4 was assigned before H3 when both were available. Comparisons
435

12
without stable H4/H3 support but with a high-information pair in any required PF10 configuration
436
were model-sensitive; the remainder were uninformative. The subsequent signal-identity audit
437
added cross-L correspondence without overwriting these historical labels.

In the post-result signal-semantics audit, signal identity was matched across L settings using exact
439
lead-pair identity or a credible-set Jaccard overlap of at least 0.50 for both traits. H4 and H3 pairs
440
were recorded separately. A comparison could therefore support at least one shared pair and still
441
contain a different H3-qualifying pair. Bayesian posterior thresholds were not interpreted as family-
442
wise error or false-discovery-rate control across the correlated comparison universe.

Corrected kriging diagnostics were evaluated for every comparison-model-trait unit: 642
445
comparisons x two QTL covariate models x two traits, for 2,568 units. Returned key structure,

expected and observed row counts and finite values were checked. Both the historical logLR>2
447
count and the source-code plotting flag (logLR>2 and abs(z)>2) were retained. All 2,568 diagnostic

units were evaluated and passed the recorded review gate; a reviewed flag was not recoded as no

anomaly. One unique official-rule event, rs1800378, was reviewed; it did not enter a disease or QTL

credible set and did not trigger a refit. This diagnostic repair occurred after the original multi-signal

Matched-input A0/A1/A2/M attribution design

We constructed four analysis arms for the frozen 642 comparisons. A0 replayed the historical ABF

calculation using the original harmonized GCST disease statistics and S_A. A1 retained those

disease statistics but restricted both traits to S_M, isolating the effect of support-set restriction at the

those counts because the affected comparisons could overlap. Strict bidirectional reclassification

ambiguous, model-sensitive or uninformative states were retained as uncertainty changes. Because

Simulation design and outcome channels
471
The frozen simulation contained 486 parameter combinations with 1,000 iterations each, for
472
486,000 primary matched-LD iterations. Summary z statistics were generated with two empirical
473
128-variant LD templates. Six scenarios were evaluated: one shared signal (S1); correlated but
474

13
distinct signals (S2); two disease signals and one QTL signal with partial sharing (S3); two signals
475
per trait with one shared pair (S4); two signals per trait with no shared pair under high LD (S5); and
476
a matched-versus-mismatched LD sensitivity scenario (S6). Disease N=24,510 and QTL N=750
477
were fixed, not varied. The 486 grid rows were six scenarios crossed with three MAF values (0.05,
478
0.20, 0.40), three target causal-pair r-squared values (0.20, 0.50, 0.80), three L values (5, 10, 20)
479
and three p12 values (1x10^-6, 1x10^-5, 1x10^-4). Each row allocated 500 iterations to each
480
empirical template.
481
The two templates used disease/QTL LD from locus 2/NK and locus 4/B_IN. Simulated summaries
482
followed z ~ Normal(sqrt(N) R b_std, R), with per-allele effects scaled by sqrt(2 MAF(1-MAF));
483
the first disease effect was log(1.12), the first QTL effect was 0.30, and second effects were -0.8
484
times the first. These were summary-z experiments rather than individual-level binary PBC
485
simulations. S6 changed only the analysis QTL LD from the same-locus PF10 to PF50 matrix,
486
preserving trait identities and variant order.

488
experiment did not directly calibrate the real-data composite gate that also required cross-L stability
489
and same-pair low-prior support. Scenario-level rates averaged the frozen MAF, LD, L and prior
490
grid; they were not error rates at a single default-prior operating point.

492

495

pair. The latter describe estimator behavior after the discovery stage and were not directly compared
497
with the ABF unconditional denominator as if they were the same estimand.

Please consider our Article, “Input matched multisignal colocalization clarifies regulatory
assignments at primary biliary cholangitis loci”, for npj Genomic Medicine.
Regulatory gene prioritization can change when colocalization inputs and signal models differ.
Using primary biliary cholangitis as a fixed disease context, we assembled a traceable PBC-wide
screen and evaluated a protocol-frozen high-information subset. The central contribution is an
empirical reliability assessment: exact input matching separates support-set and disease-statistic
changes from residual bidirectional reclassification, while signal-pair coexistence and covariate
sensitivity limit gene-level interpretation.
Truth-known simulations reveal both reduced false sharing and reduced shared-signal recovery,
with credible-set discovery reported separately. External disease-study and linked chromatin
evidence strengthen the IL12RB2 association within explicit independence and mediation limits.
Donor-level liver expression establishes detectability without corrected disease enrichment. This
combination is intended to inform defensible functional prioritization; it does not propose a
universally superior new algorithm, a newly discovered PBC gene or an established treatment
mechanism.
